published_statement: ZUREK 1985, verbatim from the page images. Abstract (p.505): 'Symmetry breaking phase transitions occurring in the early Universe are expected to leave behind long-lived topologically stable structures such as monopoles, strings or domain walls. Here I discuss the analogy between cosmological strings and vortex lines in the superfluid, and suggest a cryogenic experiment which tests key elements of the cosmological scenario for string formation. In a superfluid obtained through a rapid pressure quench, the phase of the Bose condensate wavefunction -- the 4He analogue of the broken symmetry of the field-theoretic vacuum -- will be chosen randomly in domains of some characteristic size d.' Hypotheses in the text (p.505): 'Near the second-order phase transition, the potential contribution V to the free energy density of the system can be approximated by (1)'; 'Strings will be able to form when the order parameter (Higgs field) psi is complex (2)'; 'the scenario (known as the "Kibble mechanism") for the creation of their early Universe analogues -- strings -- in nonequilibrium phase transitions is thought to involve "freezing out" of fluctuations of the Higgs field psi in the course of a rapid phase transition induced by the decrease of temperature during the cosmological expansion. The key assumption states that the phase of the frozen-out field configuration will be determined independently in regions which did not have a chance to interact.' Density (p.506): 'the density l of strings left behind by a rapid phase transition should be of the order of: l ~ d^-2 (7)'. Freeze-out (p.506): 'epsilon = (T_lambda - T)/T_lambda = t/tau_Q (11)', 'xi = xi_0 |epsilon|^-nu (12)', 'tau = xi/u = tau_0/epsilon (14)', 'tau(t^) = t^ (15)', 't^ = sqrt(tau_0 tau_Q) (16)', 'd(t^) = xi_0 (tau_Q/tau_0)^(nu/2) (17)', and 'It should be emphasized that equation (17) is only an estimate: it can be expected to yield values correct to within an order of magnitude.' Slow limit (p.506): 'had one performed the transition infinitesimally slowly, correlation length would have had time to become infinite at T = T_lambda, and d >> C would have implied v_s = 0.' Stated failure mode (p.507): 'This would indicate that either the scenario for the formation of topological defects has a flaw, or that for some reason the cosmological scenario is not applicable to 4He.' Conclusion (p.507): 'This experiment, therefore, can be regarded as a laboratory test of the Kibble mechanism, one of the key elements of the cosmological scenario.' KIBBLE 1976, READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT: see published_hypotheses; each item names the citing paper, page and wording.
published_hypotheses: Zurek 1985 (READ p.505): a SECOND-ORDER (continuous) transition: 'Near the second-order phase transition'; the freeze-out needs critical slowing down, tau = tau_0/epsilon diverging at T_lambda (eq.14, p.506).

Zurek 1985 (READ p.505): a topological condition for the defect: 'Strings will be able to form when the order parameter (Higgs field) psi is complex' (a U(1) phase with nontrivial winding: 'The winding number n ... must be an integer').
Zurek 1985 (READ p.505): the 'key assumption' of independent phase choice 'in regions which did not have a chance to interact'.

Zurek 1985 (READ p.506): a finite-rate quench; an infinitesimally slow one gives an infinite correlation length and no mismatch. Eq.(17) is an order-of-magnitude estimate by the author's own statement.

Kibble 1976 via Zurek, cond-mat/9607135 p.3, READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT: 'The kind of defects which will be left behind by the transition depends on the interplay between the symmetry which is being broken during the phase transition (more specifically, on the homotopy group of the manifold of the degenerate broken symmetry vacua) and the symmetries of the space in which the evolution is taking place (Kibble, 1976).'

Kibble 1976 via Zurek, cond-mat/9607135 p.4, READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT: 'appearance of the topological defects is -- as was observed by Kibble in his seminal paper (Kibble, 1976) -- a direct consequence of causality. In the cosmological setting the ultimate causal limit on the size of the approximately uniform patches of the new vacuum is set by the size of the horizon at the time when the transition is taking place (Kibble, 1976).'

Kibble 1976 via Zurek, cond-mat/9607135 p.4, READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT: 'In the original paper, Kibble appealed to the process of thermal activation ... Consequently, it was originally postulated that the initial density of topological effects is set by the correlation length at the Ginzburg temperature, xi(T_G) (Kibble, 1976).' (So the freeze-out scale is Zurek's, not Kibble's: p.5 'a different alternative was put forward ... the characteristic domain size should be set by the critical slowing down.')

Kibble 1976 via Zurek, cond-mat/9607135 p.26 eq.(3.6), READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT: 'l_0 = l^ ~ xi^-2, which is based on the idea that typically a piece of the vortex line will fall within a xi^-sized domain (Kibble, 1976; 1980; Vilenkin, 1981).'

Kibble 1976 via Vilenkin PRD 23 p.852 (READ from page image): 'The direction of <phi> in the manifold of degenerate vacuum states M can be different in different regions of space, and we can certainly expect it to be different in causally disconnected regions. The topology of the resulting vacuum structure is related to the topology of the manifold M, as discussed by Kibble.3 The three possible structures are vacuum domain walls, strings, and monopoles.'

Hindmarsh & Kibble, hep-ph/9411342 p.68 (READ; a restatement by Kibble himself, not attributed there to ref.[6] specifically): 'for causality reasons the phases in widely separated regions will be uncorrelated. This must be true even in a gauge theory, once the gauge ambiguity has been removed. ... (However, for a different view, see [210]).' and 'The phase transition may be first-order ... alternatively it may be a continuous, second-order process ... The net effect is much the same in both cases'.

Hindmarsh & Kibble, hep-ph/9411342 p.36 (READ) on the owner's case: 'the electroweak theory does not possess any topologically stable string solutions, because its gauge orbit space is isomorphic to S^3, which is simply connected.' and p.16: 'The standard electroweak model does not predict stable strings'.
hypothesis_drift: CONFIRMED BY READING (was computed only in the first audit): DROPPED nontrivial homotopy. warpfolder.py:77-79 'The generic output of a rapid quench through a symmetry-breaking transition is a TOPOLOGICAL DEFECT NETWORK', in the SM electroweak context of warpfolder.py:65-72. Zurek 1985 p.505 makes defect formation conditional ('Strings will be able to form when the order parameter ... is complex'); Zurek 1996 p.3 attributes the homotopy condition to Kibble 1976; Hindmarsh & Kibble p.36 state that the electroweak theory has no topologically stable strings because S^3 is simply connected. The first audit's S^3 computation (its A/B) is now backed by a read.

CONFIRMED BY READING: DROPPED a genuine continuous transition for the SCALING. Zurek 1985 p.505 'Near the second-order phase transition' and eq.(14) tau = tau_0/epsilon (critical slowing down). warpfolder.py:69 itself says 'the crossover'. Nothing read addresses a crossover; Hindmarsh & Kibble p.68 cover first- and second-order only. The domain-size law therefore has no read support in the owner's case. The owner's (b) does not use the law, only its qualitative consequence.

SOFTENED BY READING (first audit: 'WEAKENED: picks independent phases is the global-symmetry picture'): Hindmarsh & Kibble p.68 say uncorrelated phases hold 'even in a gauge theory, once the gauge ambiguity has been removed', with a dissent noted ('for a different view, see [210]', Rudaz & Srivastava, NAMED-NOT-READ). The owner's 'picks independent phases' is therefore the restated Kibble picture for gauge theories too; the first audit's gauge objection is a contested point in the literature, not a drift from the source.

UNQUANTIFIED, but now bounded by the source: 'rapid quench' (warpfolder.py:77). Zurek 1985 p.506 and Zurek 1996 p.4 ('unless the critical temperature is traversed infinitesimally slowly, the resulting broken symmetry phase will contain many distinct regions with different choices of the local vacuum') require only a quench that is not infinitesimally slow for uncorrelated domains. The owner's 'uncorrelated' clause needs no quench time; only the density law would.

ATTRIBUTION (new, from reading): the owner calls both the causal independence and the defect network 'the Kibble-Zurek mechanism'. By Zurek's own account (cond-mat/9607135 pp.4-5) Kibble 1976 supplied causality, the horizon bound, the homotopy classification and a Ginzburg-temperature scale; Zurek 1985 supplied the critical-slowing-down freeze-out. The owner uses only the part common to both, so the attribution is harmless.

lacked_data: Kibble (1976) and Zurek (1985) lacked the Higgs mass and the lattice crossover result. Reading them does not turn this into a data result. Zurek 1985 states its own scope, second-order transitions and complex order parameters, and the homotopy condition is Kibble's (via Zurek 1996 p.3). Hindmarsh & Kibble p.36 apply it to the electroweak theory with no datum: S^3 is simply connected. M's hypothesis is not supported here. The later data narrows where the tree may invoke the mechanism, not what the sources said, and the narrowing that matters (no stable EW defects) needs no data at all.
supersedes_grade: NARROWED (first audit, both sources NAMED-NOT-READ) -> NARROWED, now with Zurek 1985 READ and Kibble 1976 READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT. The grade is unchanged. One first-audit drift (gauge dependence of the phase) is softened to a contested point.
grade_evidence: Zurek 1985 (READ, Nature 317, p.505): 'Near the second-order phase transition'; 'Strings will be able to form when the order parameter (Higgs field) psi is complex'; 'The key assumption states that the phase of the frozen-out field configuration will be determined independently in regions which did not have a chance to interact.' Kibble 1976, READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT: the defect type depends 'on the homotopy group of the manifold of the degenerate broken symmetry vacua ... (Kibble, 1976)' (Zurek, cond-mat/9607135 p.3); defects are 'a direct consequence of causality' (ibid. p.4). For the owner's own case, Hindmarsh & Kibble (hep-ph/9411342 p.36): 'the electroweak theory does not possess any topologically stable string solutions, because its gauge orbit space is isomorphic to S^3, which is simply connected.' warpfolder.py:77-79 asserts a 'TOPOLOGICAL DEFECT NETWORK' as the generic output of the quench, in the electroweak context (warpfolder.py:65-72, a crossover at :69), with neither the homotopy nor the continuous-transition hypothesis. That is true on a smaller class than the tree uses it for: NARROWED. The clause that carries the owner's conclusion, 'the cooling is uncorrelated ... not a templated object', is what the sources state as their key assumption (Zurek 1985 p.505; Hindmarsh & Kibble p.68 'even in a gauge theory, once the gauge ambiguity has been removed'). So QUENCH_GIVES_A_TEMPLATED_OBJECT = False is not contradicted. It is not WRONG, and not DATA-DEPENDENT: the narrowing is topological.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: warpfolder.py:77-79 says 'uncorrelated domains, and a defect network only where the vacuum manifold has nontrivial homotopy (not the SM electroweak case)'. Zurek 1985 is now read and the Kibble content is read via restatement, so no further read is needed for STANDS. To OPEN: a reader who does not accept READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT for Kibble 1976 would leave the Kibble half OPEN. The Zurek half and Hindmarsh-Kibble p.36 would still carry NARROWED. To WRONG: a read showing that the owner's argument needs stable defects to form, or that uncorrelated domains fail at a crossover; neither was seen.
